title: Reflex logic, one more time
objective: Connect the inflammatory reflex to the general reflex-arc framework and the afferent limb.

steps.title: The same shape everywhere
steps.body: The inflammatory reflex is one more [[reflex arc]] (D8): an [[interoception|interoceptive]] **afferent** limb senses the internal state (here, inflammation), and an **efferent** limb corrects it. The knee-jerk, the baroreflex, and this all share that structure.

steps.prompt: What do the knee-jerk reflex, the baroreflex, and the inflammatory reflex share?
options: An afferent sensing limb together with an efferent corrective limb
An identical effector organ that is used in each and every single case
The complete absence of any afferent limb at all
Being driven entirely by hormones, not by nerves
steps.explanation: All are reflex arcs: sense → respond. What differs is the variable sensed and the effector, not the underlying logic.

variants.prompt: What's common to all reflex arcs?
options: An afferent limb plus an efferent limb together
The very same effector organ used each time
No afferent limb present at all within them
variants.reveal: Every reflex arc pairs an afferent (sensing) with an efferent (responding) limb.

steps.prompt: The afferent limb of the inflammatory reflex is best described as what kind of neuron?
options: An interoceptive sensory afferent reporting an internal state
An autonomic motor neuron that drives an organ to respond
A microglial cell residing inside the central nervous system
A skeletal muscle motor neuron of the somatic system
steps.explanation: The sensing side is an interoceptive afferent — the same class of neuron (vagal and spinal/DRG) at the heart of this whole app.

variants.setup: Something must sense the inflammation to start the reflex.
options: An autonomic motor neuron to an organ
A microglial cell within the brain itself
variants.reveal: The afferent limb is an interoceptive sensory neuron.

reviewNotes: Inflammatory reflex within the reflex-arc framework; afferent limb (links to afferent-limbs quiz).
